value: Anne is a tall girl.

Her hair, which is famously red, has been worn in long braids, shingled closely, and cut into short silky curls. It is also described by some as auburn or glossy, occasionally loosening into rings around her neck and forehead. She has big, luminous gray eyes that are sometimes characterized as gray-green, set against cheeks that faint flushed with pink.

label: Personality
value: Anne Shirley is characterized by an imaginative nature.
unit: Characterized by an imaginative, passionate, and serious-minded nature, she is known for her romantic worldview and a tendency to fall into daydreams. Although recognized as smart, obedient, and strong-willed, she reflects on having been heedless and impulsive in her youth. She possesses a creative gift for storytelling and writing fanciful, fairylike pieces, alongside a natural affinity for working with children. Driven by academic ambition, she has sought to win scholarships, attend college, and perform well to bring pride to those around her. Additionally, her desire to add beauty to life is paired with a deep, earnest loyalty to her friends. Despite her wisdom and maturity, she retains a youthful spirit inside.

label: History
value: Anne Shirley was brought home to Green Gables by Matthew Cuthbert.
unit: Brought home to Green Gables by Matthew Cuthbert, young orphan Anne Shirley broke down upon learning that Marilla Cuthbert expected a boy, but Marilla ultimately agreed to raise her. Anne formed an instant, lifelong bond with her neighbor Diana Barry, though she suffered several dramatic early blunders, including accidentally getting Diana drunk on currant wine and later being forced to cut her hair short after dyeing it green. Her passionate temper flared when Gilbert Blythe teased her red hair, sparking a intense academic rivalry that lasted through their shared preparation for the Queen's Entrance examination. Following Matthew's sudden death from a heart attack, Anne gave up her prestigious college scholarship to stay at Green Gables to care for Marilla and teach locally, during which time she and Gilbert finally ended their feud and became close friends. After earning her degree at Redmond College and declining marriage proposals from other suitors, Anne happily accepted Gilbert's proposal in Hester Gray's garden. Upon marrying, the couple moved into a small house at Four Winds Harbor, where Anne endured the tragic loss of her firstborn infant daughter, Joyce, before giving birth to a healthy son named James Matthew. Over time, the family expanded and relocated to a larger home in Glen St. Mary called Ingleside, where Anne managed her bustling household alongside her loyal housekeeper Susan Baker. Though her later years were defined by raising her children and participating in local village affairs, Anne remained a loving, supportive mother when her son Walter engaged in a physical fight to defend her honor.

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "Pretty well. I imagine a good deal, and that helps to pass the time. Of course, it’s rather lonesome. But then, I may as well get used to that."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "I don’t get cross about other things; but I’m so tired of being twitted about my hair and it just makes me boil right over. Do you suppose my hair will really be a handsome auburn when I grow up?"

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "I love pretty things; and I hate to look in the glass and see something that isn’t pretty. It makes me feel so sorrowful—just as I feel when I look at any ugly thing. I pity it because it isn’t beautiful."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "I love Green Gables already, and I never loved any place before. No place ever seemed like home. Oh, Marilla, I’m so happy. I could pray right now and not find it a bit hard."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "Oh, Marilla, I’m frightened—now that it has come I’m actually frightened. What if she shouldn’t like me! It would be the most tragical disappointment of my life."

label: History
value: Aunt Jamesina was named after James.
unit: Aunt Jamesina was named after her father, James, who drowned at sea shortly before her birth, and she grew up wishing for a yellow silk dress that neither her mother nor her husband permitted her to have. Known for teasing her suitors in her youth, she taught her daughter to cook before college and prayed for her to become a missionary. Later in life, she moved into Patty's Place alongside her cats, Joseph and the Sarah-cat, to chaperon Anne Shirley and her friends during their college years. Over the course of their time together, she managed the household, shared her pragmatic yet humorous views on life and love, and offered a grounding presence through the girls' academic studies, social gatherings, and romantic entanglements. At the end of their four years of college, she reflected with the household on the enduring value of common sense and life lessons before the group dissolved Patty's Place upon graduation.

value: Aunt Jamesina said: "Kittens have to be drowned, I admit, or the world would be overrun. But no decent, grown-up cat should be done to death—unless he sucks eggs."

label: Quote
value: Aunt Jamesina said: "Well, I hope so, Anne. I do hope so, because I love her. But I can’t understand her—she beats me. She isn’t like any of the girls I ever knew, or any of the girls I was myself."

label: Quote
value: Aunt Jamesina said: "Yes, in my soul. But I’ll admit my legs aren’t as young as yours. You go and get some fresh air, Anne. You look pale lately."

label: Quote
value: Aunt Jamesina said: "Anybody is liable to rheumatism in her legs, Anne. It’s only old people who should have rheumatism in their souls, though. Thank goodness, I never have. When you get rheumatism in your soul you might as well go and pick out your coffin."

label: Quote
value: Aunt Jamesina said: "I’ve got them yet. There are three old widowers at home who have been casting sheep’s eyes at me for some time. You children needn’t think you own all the romance in the world."

label: History
value: Carl lived in Maywater.
unit: Carl lived in Maywater before moving to the Glen with his family. After meeting the Blythe children in Rainbow Valley, Carl and his siblings quickly bonded with them and formed a close friendship. He later joined his siblings and the Blythes in forming the Good-Conduct Club to manage their behavior and impose self-punishments to protect their father's reputation. As part of a club punishment, Carl mistook a local woman under a sheet for a ghost while in Rainbow Valley, resulting in a mortifying flight to safety. Jerry then ordered Carl to sit alone in the graveyard until midnight as a penalty for cowardice; Carl completed the task during a chilling rainstorm, which caused him to contract a severe case of pneumonia that he narrowly survived under Dr. Blythe's care. Following his recovery, Carl put an eel in Mrs. Carr's buggy, but when his father attempted to whip him as punishment, his father broke down upon looking into Carl's eyes and spared him.

label: History
value: Charlotta the Fourth worked as a young helper for Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge.
unit: Charlotta the Fourth worked as a young helper and maid for Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge, where she assisted with household duties, picked strawberries, and expressed deep concern when her employer was feeling unusually despondent. Following the resolution of Miss Lavendar's romance, Charlotta excitedly prepared for a move to Boston and helped tidy Echo Lodge after Miss Lavendar's garden wedding. Years later, she returned to Green Gables as one of the guests attending Anne's wedding, and she eventually married a good-tempered American bricklayer named Tom.

label: History
value: Cornelia Bryant was a frequent guest at Anne and Gilbert Blythe's home in Four Winds Harbor
unit: Cornelia Bryant was frequent guest at Anne and Gilbert Blythe's home in Four Winds Harbor, often sharing her sharp opinions on local men, religion, and town news. After learning the tragic history of Leslie Moore, she encouraged Anne to be a persistent friend to her. When Gilbert suggested sending Leslie's brain-damaged husband, Dick, to Montreal for a medical evaluation, Cornelia initially confronted Anne in anger, though she ultimately accepted the plan. She was utterly shocked when the surgery revealed that Dick was actually his cousin, George Moore, which freed Leslie from her tragic marriage. Later, Cornelia surprised her friends by revealing her intention to marry Marshall Elliott, and she subsequently became Mrs. Marshall Elliott. Years later, after returning from a trip to Europe, Cornelia caught up with Anne and Susan Baker at Ingleside to discuss the new minister, Mr. Meredith, and his motherless children. Upon learning that Mary Vance's abusive former guardian had died, Cornelia was approached by Una Meredith and agreed to adopt Mary after consulting with Marshall. Despite occasionally expressing dismay over the Meredith children's scandals, Cornelia was swayed by Anne to take pride in the minister's family, and she continued to visit Ingleside to gossip about town affairs and upcoming weddings.

label: Personality
value: Davy is a mischievous youth.
unit: Davy is a mischievous, disobedient, and lively youth who possesses an innate knack for winning love despite his heedless and forgetful nature. Driven by intense curiosity, he frequently asks inquisitive questions and delights in making terrible faces. Practical and devoid of imagination, he works with overzealous energy, prefers bloodthirsty stories, and is easily comforted by plum jam. Though previously known for his misbehavior, he has developed into a smart boy and is considered a reformed character. His ambitions include becoming a storekeeper to hoard sweets, living to be a hundred years old, and seeing the stone gods at the lighthouse.

label: History
value: Davy Keith lost his father as an infant.
unit: Davy Keith lost his father as an infant and was raised without proper guidance, developing a reputation as a holy terror for mischief before arriving at Green Gables with his twin sister Dora. Shortly after his arrival, Davy locked Dora in a toolhouse, but he tearfully promised never to lie again after realizing he had made Anne Shirley cry. Despite his persistent troublemaking—such as stealing jam and accidentally ruining lemon pies meant for a guest—Marilla Cuthbert and Anne developed a fond affection for him. Davy's permanent stay at Green Gables was secured when word arrived that Richard Keith had died and left money in trust for the twins. Over time, Davy looked to Anne for comfort and guidance, expressing a deep fondness for her, confessing his jealousies, and admitting his struggles with bad language and guilty conscience when he broke rules. Later in his youth, he convinced Dora to skip Sunday School to go fishing, but he ultimately confessed his misdeeds and lies to Anne. Though Davy continued his lively antics, he showed significant growth in behavior and maturity as he grew older.

Shortly after his arrival, Davy locked Dora in a toolhouse, but he tearfully promised never to lie again after realizing he had made Anne Shirley cry. Despite his persistent troublemaking—such as stealing jam and accidentally ruining lemon pies meant for a guest—Marilla Cuthbert and Anne developed a fond affection for him. Davy's permanent stay at Green Gables was secured when word arrived that Richard Keith had died and left money in trust for the twins. Over time, Davy looked to Anne for comfort and guidance, expressing a deep fondness for her, confessing his jealousies, and admitting his struggles with bad language and guilty conscience when he broke rules. Later in his youth, he convinced Dora to skip Sunday School to go fishing, but he ultimately confessed his misdeeds and lies to Anne. Though Davy continued his lively antics, he showed significant growth in behavior and maturity as he grew older.

value: Davy Keith said: "I just did it for fun. Things have been so awful quiet here for so long that I thought it would be fun to give you folks a big scare. It was, too."

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: “I never will, now that I know it’s bad,” asseverated Davy between sobs. “If you ever catch me telling a whopper again you can . . .” Davy groped mentally for a suitable penance . . . “you can skin me alive, Anne.”

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: “Why?” queried Davy, settling comfortably down and looking up with a tearstained, investigating face. “Why ain’t whopper as good as falsehood? I want to know. It’s just as big a word.”

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: “Then,” said Davy decidedly, “Marilla is bad, for she tells them. And she’s worse’n me, for I didn’t know it was wrong but she does.”

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: “But I tell you there is,” persisted Davy. “It was in that question Marilla taught me last Sunday. ‘Why should we love God?’ It says, ‘Because He makes preserves, and redeems us.’ Preserves is just a holy way of saying jam.”

label: History
value: Diana Barry was named by a schoolmaster.
unit: Diana Barry was named by a schoolmaster who was boarding with her family when she was born. During her youth, she met Anne Shirley at Orchard Slope, where they pledged eternal friendship, and they frequently signaled to each other across distance using candle flashes. The girls attended school together, where Diana welcomed Anne back after Anne was temporarily forbidden to play with her and when Anne refused to attend school following a punishment. Diana also accompanied Anne on local outings, such as canvassing for the Village Improvement Society, searching for a willow-ware platter at Spencervale, and discovering Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge. Over the years, Diana served as a trusted confidante for Anne's creative pursuits, including the creation of a story club in their youth and reviewing Anne's written story, Averil's Atonement. As they grew older, Diana became engaged to Fred Wright, and Anne served as a helper when Diana married Fred at Orchard Slope. Four years after her marriage, Diana gave birth to a baby boy.

value: Dick Moore inherited a sea-going streak from his mother.
unit: Dick Moore inherited a sea-going streak from his mother and divided his time between sailing in the summer, working in his father's store in the winter, and owning a dog named Carlo. He settled with Leslie on the West place for a winter, but he was a drunkard who went to Nova Scotia to visit relatives before dying of yellow fever in Cuba thirteen years prior. A letter eventually revealed that the man long believed to be Dick was actually his lookalike cousin, George Moore.

Following the death of Richard Keith, money was left in trust for Dora and her brother, allowing them to remain permanently at Green Gables. She later attended school, where she was once frightened by a classmate's ghost stories, and was eventually persuaded by Davy to skip Sunday School to go fishing.

value: Ellen West discussed European politics.

Later, after Norman Douglas asked to marry Ellen, Rosemary agreed to release her from her promise, but Ellen ultimately refused to marry Norman after realizing it would leave Rosemary living alone.

label: History
value: Faith Meredith moved to Glen St. Mary
unit: Faith Meredith moved to Glen St. Mary from Maywater, where she had been given a pet rooster named Adam as a chick. After arriving in the Glen, she and her siblings befriended the Blythe children in Rainbow Valley and helped house a runaway orphan named Mary Vance. Due to losing track of the days, Faith and her sister Una accidentally performed their household chores on a Sunday, sparking a local scandal. Faith attempted to compensate for her mistake by addressing the church congregation, and she later rode pigs through the Glen on a dare with Walter Blythe. Upon learning that her father's position in the ministry was endangered by a lack of financial support, Faith confronted the eccentric Norman Douglas and persuaded him to attend church and contribute to her father's salary. When her pet rooster Adam was killed to feed a visiting minister, Faith expressed her anger by allowing the minister's coat-tails to catch fire, though she was later comforted by Rosemary West. Following repeated public embarrassments, Faith joined her siblings in forming a self-disciplining Good-Conduct Club. After giving her good stockings to a needy girl, Faith attended church bare-legged to avoid wearing striped stockings, causing another scandal which she attempted to resolve by writing a letter of explanation to the local newspaper.

label: History
value: Faith attempted to resolve the scandal by writing a letter of explanation to the local newspaper.
unit: Faith Meredith moved to Glen St. Mary from Maywater, where she had been given a pet rooster named Adam as a chick. After arriving in the Glen, she and her siblings befriended the Blythe children in Rainbow Valley and helped house a runaway orphan named Mary Vance. Due to losing track of the days, Faith and her sister Una accidentally performed their household chores on a Sunday, sparking a local scandal. Faith attempted to compensate for her mistake by addressing the church congregation, and she later rode pigs through the Glen on a dare with Walter Blythe. Upon learning that her father's position in the ministry was endangered by a lack of financial support, Faith confronted the eccentric Norman Douglas and persuaded him to attend church and contribute to her father's salary. label: Quote
value: Faith said: "Here, Una, you stir it while I set the table. If I leave it for a minute the horrid stuff will burn. It’s half past nine. We’ll be late for Sunday School."

label: Quote
value: Faith said: "I’d hate to think the Methodists were better at going to Sunday School on rainy Sundays than the Presbyterians. But there’s no preaching in their Church to-day, either, so likely their Sunday School is in the afternoon."

label: Quote
value: Faith said: "I like being myself. It’s more interesting. Jessie Drew is as good a housekeeper as her mother, but would you want to be as stupid as she is?"

label: Quote
value: Faith said: "Just as soon as you get fond of a place you are torn up by the roots. I’ll never, never, never marry a minister, no matter how nice he is."

label: Quote
value: Faith said: "I love birds. Only—would Aunt Martha’s cat eat it? It’s so tragic to have your pets eaten. I don’t think I could endure it a second time."

label: History
value: Gilbert Blythe spent three years in Alberta with his sick father.
unit: After spending three years in Alberta with his sick father and a summer visiting cousins in New Brunswick, Gilbert Blythe returned to Avonlea, where he pulled Anne Shirley's braid on his first day back at school, prompting her to break a slate over his head and refuse his apology. Over the next few years, Gilbert maintained a fierce academic rivalry with Anne while co-founding the Avonlea Village Improvement Society alongside her. He saved her life when her boat began to sink on the pond, and he later gave up the Avonlea school contract so that she could take the local teaching job near home. During their time as local teachers, Gilbert and Anne put in two years of steady work preparing for college and eventually became close friends. They both attended Redmond College in Kingsport, where Gilbert led the freshman class to victory in the annual Arts Rush. During their time in college, Gilbert proposed marriage to Anne, but she rejected him, causing a temporary breach in their friendship. Shortly after recovering from a life-threatening bout of typhoid fever, Gilbert proposed to Anne once again, and she happily accepted. After their wedding at Green Gables, Gilbert carried Anne across the threshold of their new home in Four Winds Harbor and established his medical practice. When a local man named Dick Moore lost his memory, Gilbert insisted on pursuing a surgical option that ultimately led to the discovery of the man's true identity as George Moore. Gilbert and Anne welcomed the birth of their healthy son, James Matthew, though their first child, Joyce, had passed away shortly after birth. Eventually, Gilbert proposed purchasing the Morgan place in Glen St. Mary, leading the family to relocate to Ingleside, where he continued his work as the town's doctor.

He is frequently seen smoking a pipe on his veranda, and those around him have noted that he seems much changed and twice as nice since getting married.

label: History
value: Before settling in Avonlea, Harrison visited Prince Edward Island as a boy.
unit: Before settling in Avonlea, Harrison visited Prince Edward Island as a boy and spent time living in Scottsford, New Brunswick. Following the death of his sister, he kept a bachelor's hall and eventually promised her on her deathbed that he would marry. He subsequently wed Emily Scott and went on a fortnight's wedding trip to St. John. After moving to Avonlea as Anne Shirley's neighbor, Harrison angrily confronted her when her cow strayed into his oat field, but the two established an unexpected friendship after Anne mistakenly sold his Jersey cow and came to confess and trade cows over tea and cake. Harrison expressed doubt over Anne's non-violent teaching philosophy and later flatly refused her request for a donation to the Village Improvement Society. Following a severe thunderstorm that killed his parrot, Harrison explained to Anne the history of his marriage and his past falling out with Emily, who shortly thereafter reunited with him in Avonlea. He continued to act as a neighborly confidant, providing feedback on Anne's story Averil's Atonement, encouraging her not to give up on writing after initial magazine rejections, and later hinting at a story competition.

value: Jane Andrews is a sensible individual.
unit: Jane Andrews is a sensible, practical, and lady-like individual known for her unflappable, placid, and amiable temperament. Characterized as neat, plain, and conscientious, she is a deliberate plodder in her pursuits. As an educator, she maintains a strict approach, punishing her pupils for making funny speeches. She possesses notable skills in domestic science and cooking. Her early career motivations centered on dedicated teaching, earning her salary fairly, pleasing school trustees, and achieving recognition on the inspector's roll of honor.

Following the eventual death of John's mother, John proposed to Janet, revealing he had been bound by a promise to his mother to wait until after her passing before marrying or telling anyone.

label: Quote
value: Janet said: "If she wasn’t—but she is. So we mustn’t speak evil of her. But I’m happy at last, Anne. And I wouldn’t have minded waiting so long a bit if I’d only known why."

label: Quote
value: Janet said: "Oh, she does. She’s told me time and again that she’d love to see John settled before her time comes. She’s always giving him hints—you heard her yourself the other day. I thought I’d ha’ gone through the floor."

label: Quote
value: Janet said: “I couldn’t,” said poor Janet pathetically. “You see, Anne, I’ve always been awful fond of John. He might just as well keep coming as not, for there was never anybody else I’d want, so it didn’t matter.”

value: Janet said: "No, I guess not. I was afraid to try, anyway, for fear he’d think I meant it and just go. I suppose I’m a poor-spirited creature, but that is how I feel. And I can’t help it."

label: History
value: Jem Blythe stuck out his tongue at Mrs. Alec Davis.
unit: Jem Blythe once stuck out his tongue at Mrs. Alec Davis, causing her to refuse to employ his father again. The previous summer, he suffered a foot injury that caused his family great distress, and he was also bequeathed a museum of curios by Captain Jim Boyd. After moving to a new home in the Glen with his family, Jem cooked caught trout during an evening picnic in Rainbow Valley with his siblings, where they soon met and befriended the Meredith children. Later, when the Meredith children faced local scandal, Jem joined them in the graveyard and suggested they form a Good-Conduct Club so they could discipline themselves. On his final evening before leaving home to attend Queen's Academy, Jem gathered with the other children in Rainbow Valley, speaking with Walter about battles and following the Pied Piper's call into the future.

label: History
value: Jerry Corcoran offered a political bribe to Judson Parker.
unit: Jerry Corcoran offered a political bribe to Judson Parker, which was accidentally overheard by Anne Shirley. Later, as one of the Meredith children living at the manse, Jerry joined his siblings Faith, Una, and Carl in forming the Good-Conduct Club alongside Jem Blythe to manage their behavior and avoid bringing dishonor to their father. When Faith attempted to catch a cold on a snowbank to avoid wearing ugly stockings to church, Jerry and Una forcibly pulled her off. After Faith caused a scandal by attending church without stockings, Jerry enforced a Good-Conduct Club punishment requiring her to wear the hated pair. Jerry later assigned a club punishment to Carl for cowardice, ordering him to sit in the graveyard until midnight; though Carl completed the task, he contracted severe pneumonia as a result before eventually recovering.

label: History
value: Lavendar Lewis lived at Echo Lodge
unit: Miss Lavendar Lewis lived at Echo Lodge alongside her young helper, Charlotta the Fourth. After Anne Shirley and Diana Barry accidentally discovered her home during a walk, Miss Lavendar hosted them for tea and heard mention of Paul Irving, the son of her former fiancé, Stephen Irving. Following a later visit where she recounted her past romance and quarrel with Stephen to Anne, Miss Lavendar met Paul and formed a fond friendship with him. Months later, Anne delivered a note to Miss Lavendar from Stephen, prompting a meeting at Echo Lodge where Miss Lavendar and Stephen reconciled. The pair were subsequently married in an intimate ceremony in her garden. In later years, Miss Lavendar hosted Anne during summer vacations, where Anne confided in her about refusing Gilbert Blythe's marriage proposal.

value: Lavendar Lewis said: "But oh, won’t you stay and have tea with me? Please, do. Mr. Kimball’s will have tea over before you get there. And Charlotta the Fourth and I will be so glad to have you."

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "to believe I’m old. Now, who are you . . . just for convenience’ sake? Diana Barry? And Anne Shirley? May I pretend that I’ve known you for a hundred years and call you Anne and Diana right away?"

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "I love them myself. They are very good company . . . with a little pretending. On calm evenings Charlotta the Fourth and I often sit out here and amuse ourselves with them. Charlotta, take back the horn and hang it carefully in its place."

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "It gave me a shock to hear about Stephen’s son that first day you were here, Anne. I’ve never been able to mention him to you since, but I’ve wanted to know all about him. What sort of a boy is he?"

value: Leslie Moore possesses a clever personality.

More recently, a notable change has come over her, leaving her laughing and cheerful. Gifted in dancing and exquisite handwork such as delicate embroidery, her ambitions include working to make money to shingle her roof, wishing to be a mother, and intending to move to Montreal to pursue nursing.

label: History
value: Leslie Moore is the daughter of Frank West
unit: The daughter of Frank West and Rose Elliott, Leslie Moore experienced a tragic youth, finding her father after he committed suicide when she was fourteen, and losing her four-year-younger brother Kenneth to a farm accident when she was twelve. Coerced into marrying Dick Moore at sixteen to save her mother's home from mortgage foreclosure, Leslie subsequently lost her mother to pneumonia the following spring. Despite her difficult circumstances, she inherited money from her grandmother West to attend Queen's Academy, where she completed two years of coursework in a single year to earn her First, before returning home to teach at the Glen school. Leslie formed a friendship with Anne Blythe at Four Winds, eventually confessing to Anne that she had initially felt intense envy and resentment toward her happiness before the two reconciled. When writer Owen Ford stayed at her home as a boarder while adapting Captain Jim's life story into a novel, Leslie developed deep feelings for him and tearfully confessed her love to Anne when he departed. Gilbert Blythe later informed Leslie of a potential medical operation for Dick; she secured a mortgage from Captain Jim to take him to Montreal, where the surgery revealed that the man was actually Dick's lookalike cousin, George Moore, and that her husband had died years prior. Freed from her marriage, Leslie stayed with Anne and Gilbert when Owen returned to Four Winds, leading Owen to declare his love for her, which she eagerly returned. Afterward, Leslie comforted Anne during her move to the Glen by sharing that Owen planned to purchase the house of dreams as a summer home.

label: Quote
value: Leslie Moore said: “I ENVY Anne,” said Leslie suddenly and fiercely, “and I’d envy her even if she had died! She was a mother for one beautiful day. I’d gladly give my life for THAT!”

label: Quote
value: Leslie Moore said: "If I had known I would have gone away—I wouldn’t have stayed here to meet him. You should have told me. It wasn’t fair of you, Anne—oh, it wasn’t fair!"

label: Quote
value: Leslie Moore said: "Anne likes the pink ones best, and Gilbert likes the white. But I want the crimson ones. They satisfy some craving in me as no other flower does."

label: Quote
value: Leslie Moore said: "It seems too great to be real—I’m afraid to speak of it—to think of it. It seems to me that it must just be another dream of this house of dreams and it will vanish when I leave here."

label: Quote
value: Leslie Moore said: "And, oh! I have such good news. He writes me that he is going to buy this place from the church trustees and keep it to spend our summer vacations in. Anne, are you not glad?"

label: History
value: Marilla Cuthbert raised Anne Shirley at Green Gables.
unit: Marilla Cuthbert raised Anne Shirley at Green Gables after adopting her fourteen years earlier, despite having lived there for sixty years and never traveling more than sixty miles from home. Having been raised under traditional childhood discipline and kept still when told as a child, Marilla initially reacted with shock when Matthew brought home a girl instead of a boy. Though she intended to return Anne, Marilla felt pity upon learning of the child's past hardships and resolved to raise and educate her properly. Over time, she developed a deep affection for Anne, comforting her through various mishaps, encouraging her education, and proudly supporting her success on the Queen's Entrance examination. Following Matthew's sudden death and receiving news from an oculist that she faced potential blindness, Marilla was spared selling Green Gables when Anne chose to forego college to stay and teach locally. Later, Marilla took in her orphaned twin cousins, Davy and Dora Keith, enduring a hectic first six months with Davy's unruly behavior before deciding to keep them permanently. To enable Anne to attend Redmond College without worrying about the household, Marilla invited the newly widowed Rachel Lynde to move into Green Gables. Marilla eventually celebrated Anne's marriage to Gilbert Blythe, and she traveled to Four Winds to attend their first Christmas dinner and support Anne through the heartbreaking loss of her first baby.

label: History
value: Marshall Elliott was a noted dancer in his youth.
unit: In his youth, Marshall Elliott was a noted dancer who vowed not to cut his hair or shave until the Liberals won power. Years later, he attended a New Year's Eve celebration at the Four Winds lighthouse, where he danced around the fire with Leslie. After the Liberals eventually won the general election, Marshall fulfilled his vow and shaved his beard. Later, when Cornelia Bryant was asked to adopt Mary Vance, she agreed to take the girl after consulting with Marshall.

label: History
value: Mary Vance is a runaway orphan
unit: Mary Vance, a runaway orphan who had been abused by her former guardian Mrs. Wiley, was found starving in a barn loft by the Meredith children. They brought her to the manse, where she was fed, given clean clothes, and accommodated in the garret. She quickly settled into life at the manse, taking over housecleaning duties and spending time with the local children in Rainbow Valley. After learning that Mrs. Wiley had died, Mary was adopted by Cornelia Bryant upon Una Meredith's intervention. Settling into her new home, Mary often shared neighborhood gossip, warnings, and stories with the Meredith and Blythe children, while boasting of her upgraded wardrobe. On various occasions, she warned Una about the prospect of her father remarrying, informed Faith about threats to Mr. Meredith's pastoral position, and lectured the children on how their wild behavior caused public scandal.

unit: Mary Vance, a runaway orphan who had been abused by her former guardian Mrs. Wiley, was found starving in a barn loft by the Meredith children. They brought her to the manse, where she was fed, given clean clothes, and accommodated in the garret. She quickly settled into life at the manse, taking over housecleaning duties and spending time with the local children in Rainbow Valley. After learning that Mrs. Wiley had died, Mary was adopted by Cornelia Bryant upon Una Meredith's intervention. Settling into her new home, Mary often shared neighborhood gossip, warnings, and stories with the Meredith and Blythe children, while boasting of her upgraded wardrobe. On various occasions, she warned Una about the prospect of her father remarrying, informed Faith about threats to Mr. Meredith's pastoral position, and lectured the children on how their wild behavior caused public scandal.

label: Quote
value: Mary Vance said: "You think you’re something, don’t you, all dressed up like a doll! Look at me. My dress is all rags and I don’t care! I’d rather be ragged than a doll baby. Go home and tell them to put you in a glass case. Look at me—look at me—look at me!"

label: Quote
value: Mary Vance said: “That yarn about the divining rod is no lie, anyhow,” said Mary. “Old Jake Crawford over-harbour can work it. They send for him from everywhere when they want to dig a well. And I believe I know the Wandering Jew.”

label: Quote
value: Mary Vance said: "That slipped out ‘fore I thought—it did, honest to—I mean, true’s you live, and I swallowed half of it. You folks over here are mighty squeamish seems to me. Wish you could have heard the Wileys when they had a fight."

label: Quote
value: Mary Vance said: “I ain’t a lady,” said Mary. “What chance’ve I ever had of being a lady? But I won’t say that again if I can help it. I promise you.”

label: Quote
value: Mary Vance said: “I don’t expect Him to answer ‘em anyhow,” said Mary of little faith. “I’ve been asking Him for a week to clear up this Wiley affair and He hasn’t done a thing. I’m going to give up.”

label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert was an extremely shy man.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert was an extremely shy man who dreaded almost all women except his sister Marilla and Mrs. Rachel Lynde. Due to his quiet nature, he rarely left home, and local boys found it difficult to get acquainted with him. When Matthew went to Bright River station to pick up an orphan boy to help on the farm, he was surprised to find a talkative young girl named Anne instead. Although Marilla initially intended to send Anne back, Matthew gently advocated for keeping her. As Anne settled into Green Gables, Matthew showed her quiet kindness, bringing her sweeties and offering warm encouragement for her schoolwork. Observing that Anne lacked stylish clothing like her peers, he sought the help of Mrs. Lynde to secure a brown dress with puffed sleeves for her as a Christmas gift. Over the years, he took immense pride in Anne's academic achievements, including her entrance into Queen's Academy and her winning of the Avery Scholarship. Following Anne's return home, Matthew's health began to fail. Shortly thereafter, he suffered a fatal collapse after reading news of a bank failure, leaving Marilla and Anne to mourn his loss.

label: History
value: Norman Douglas went about with Ellen West for two years
unit: In his youth, Norman Douglas went about with Ellen West for two years before quitting her in a fit of pique and marrying Hester Reese out of temper. He spent twenty years away from church after a session member cheated him in a cow deal, and he buried his wife ten years after his marriage. Decades later, Faith Meredith boldly confronted him, leading him to apologize and agree to attend church monthly and contribute to the minister's salary. He later attended a party where he engaged in a lively argument with Ellen. Desiring to marry Ellen, Norman confronted her sister Rosemary in Rainbow Valley and secured her release of Ellen's past promise, though the marriage was stymied when Ellen refused to leave Rosemary living alone.

label: Quote
value: Norman Douglas said: "Well, a bargain is a bargain. I reckon I can stand it twelve times a year. What a sensation it’ll make the first Sunday I go! And old Susan Baker says I’m going to hell, hey? Do you believe I’ll go there—come, now, do you?"

label: Quote
value: Norman Douglas said: "Hey, Wilson, haven’t you got a smile on yet? Beats all how you women can sulk! I never sulked in my life—it’s just one big flash and crash with me and then—pouf—the squall’s over and the sun is out and you could eat out of my hand."

label: Quote
value: Norman Douglas said: "Listen to her. You can’t cuddle a rooster as you can a kitten. Who ever heard of petting a rooster? Better take little Tom. I want to find a good home for him."

label: Quote
value: Norman Douglas said: "I can’t stand snivelling. If you’ve anything to say, say it and have done. Great Kitty, is the girl possessed of a dumb spirit? Don’t look at me like that—I’m human—I haven’t got a tail! Who are you—who are you, I say?"

label: Quote
value: Norman Douglas said: "‘Evening, girl. Sit down again—sit down again. I want to have a talk with you. Bless the girl, what’s she looking at me like that for? I don’t want to eat you—I’ve had my supper. Sit down and be civil."

label: History
value: Owen Ford was a newspaper writer.
unit: Owen Ford was a newspaper writer and magazine short-story author who traveled to Four Winds to recover from a spring bout of typhoid fever and find inspiration for a novel. After meeting Anne Shirley and boarding at Leslie Moore's house, he visited Captain Jim, who shared his treasured life-book and inspired Owen to write a novel based on the captain's life and tales. Throughout a summer spent writing the manuscript alongside Anne, Leslie, and Captain Jim, Owen fell deeply in love with Leslie, though he initially agonized over leaving her behind due to her circumstances. Upon returning to Four Winds for a visit, Owen declared his love to Leslie in the garden, and she confessed her love for him in return, receiving a heartwarming benediction from Captain Jim.

label: History
value: Paul Irving was a young schoolboy in Avonlea.
unit: Paul Irving was once a young schoolboy in Avonlea who had lost his mother three years prior. He was an imaginative student under Anne Shirley's instruction, comforting her early on with wild orchids and sharing stories of his imaginary shore friends and rock people. As his teacher, Anne spent considerable time with Paul, listening to his creative thoughts and visiting Echo Lodge with him, where he bonded with Miss Lavendar over their shared dream-people. Paul was distressed upon learning that Anne was resigning from her teaching post to attend college. After his father, Stephen Irving, returned to marry Miss Lavendar, Paul expressed excitement about moving to Boston. Years later, he returned as a guest to attend Anne and Gilbert's wedding at Green Gables.

As his teacher, Anne spent considerable time with Paul, listening to his creative thoughts and visiting Echo Lodge with him, where he bonded with Miss Lavendar over their shared dream-people. Paul was distressed upon learning that Anne was resigning from her teaching post to attend college. After his father, Stephen Irving, returned to marry Miss Lavendar, Paul expressed excitement about moving to Boston. Years later, he returned as a guest to attend Anne and Gilbert's wedding at Green Gables.

label: Quote
value: Paul Irving said: "and I came back to give them to you because I thought you were the kind of lady that would like them, and because . . ."

label: Quote
value: Paul Irving said: “Yes; but if dryads are foolish they must take the consequences, just as if they were real people,” said Paul gravely. “Do you know what I think about the new moon, teacher? I think it is a little golden boat full of dreams.”

label: Quote
value: Paul Irving said: "I’ve eaten enough to make anyone grow. I do hope, now that I’ve begun, I’ll keep on till I’m as tall as father. He is six feet, you know, Miss Lavendar."

label: Quote
value: Paul Irving said: "I think you would make a splendid mother. You have just the right look in your eyes . . . the look my little mother always had. I think it’s a pity you haven’t any boys of your own."

label: Quote
value: Paul Irving said: "you can’t think what has happened! Something so splendid. Father is here . . . just think of that! Father is here! Come right in. Father, this is my beautiful teacher. You know, father."

value: Philippa Gordon is the daughter of a prominent man from a Bluenose family in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia.
unit: Philippa Gordon, the daughter of a prominent man from a Bluenose family in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, first met Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant while exploring Old St. John's Cemetery near Redmond College. She quickly adopted them into her social circle and eventually persuaded them to let her join their household at Patty's Place. While spending a summer at a boardinghouse, Phil met a divinity student named Jonas Blake, whose sermon deeply moved her and inspired feelings of love. She later accepted Jonas's marriage proposal and shared the news with Anne. After graduating from Redmond College, Phil comforted Anne when Anne rejected Royal Gardner's marriage proposal. Phil subsequently married Jonas, with Anne serving as her bridesmaid. Years later, Phil returned to Green Gables as a guest to attend Anne and Gilbert's wedding.

label: Quote
value: Phil Gordon said: "I’ll go, if I can walk with Priscilla and Charlie. That will be a bearable degree of gooseberry. That Gilbert of yours is a darling, Anne, but why does he go around so much with Goggle-eyes?"

label: Quote
value: Phil Gordon said: "I don’t want William’s Island especially, but I’m sure I couldn’t get it if I did. Look at that sentry on the summit of the fort, right beside the flag. Doesn’t he look as if he had stepped out of a romance?"

label: Quote
value: Phil Gordon said: "Look—in white letters, around the archway over the gate. ‘Patty’s Place.’ Isn’t that killing? Especially on this Avenue of Pinehursts and Elmwolds and Cedarcrofts? ‘Patty’s Place,’ if you please! I adore it."

label: Quote
value: Phil Gordon said: "Joseph, you calico beastie, don’t you dare jump on my lap. I won’t go to a dance all over cat hairs. No, Anne, I won’t look matronly. But no doubt I’ll be married."

label: Quote
value: Phil Gordon said: "No, he would do if he wasn’t poor. I must marry a rich man, Aunt Jamesina. That—and good looks—is an indispensable qualification. I’d marry Gilbert Blythe if he were rich."

label: History
value: Phillips is a local schoolteacher.
unit: As a local schoolteacher who boarded at Eben Wright's house, Phillips was known for frequently whipping his students and maintaining poor order in his classroom. When Gilbert Blythe teased Anne Shirley, prompting her to smash her slate over Gilbert's head, Phillips punished Anne by making her stand at the blackboard. Later, Phillips publicly disciplined Anne for being late by forcing her to sit next to Gilbert, an act that drove Anne to temporarily quit attending his school.

label: History
value: Priscilla Grant attended Queen's school
unit: Priscilla Grant attended Queen's school with Anne Shirley and was the niece of author Mrs. Charlotte E. Morgan. During a spring picnic walk in Avonlea with her friends, she poetically imagined nature alongside Anne while exploring the hidden garden of Hester Gray. She later surprised Anne with an unexpected visit to Green Gables, bringing her aunt Mrs. Morgan along for dinner. Priscilla went on to study at Redmond College, greeting Anne upon her arrival in Kingsport and helping her settle into college life. She helped establish a shared household at Patty's Place with Anne, Stella Maynard, and Philippa Gordon, living there together throughout their remaining years at Redmond. She eventually married a handsome foreign missionary.

label: Personality
value: Rachel Lynde is a capable woman.
unit: A capable and farseeing woman, she is a remarkably active worker in church affairs who is deeply committed to her duties. Known for being outspoken, opinionated, and a bit officious, she prides herself on speaking her mind without hesitation and is an eager judge of human nature and housekeeping. Though she can be bossy, critical, and gossipy, she remains a genuinely kindly and generous soul who is easily shocked by naughtiness. Her worldview includes a belief in foreordination and a strong skepticism toward higher education for women as well as the writing of fiction. Furthermore, she is a red-hot politician who keeps a sharp eye on local happenings and is always eager to offer advice. In addition to her social and community involvement, she possesses practical skills in sewing, dressmaking, and knitting cotton-warp quilts.

A long-standing housekeeper in Avonlea who knitted sixteen cotton warp quilts, she lived as a neighbor to Marilla Cuthbert for forty-five years without ever having a quarrel. label: History
value: At seventeen, Rosemary West was engaged to a young sailor.
unit: At seventeen, Rosemary West was engaged to a young sailor who subsequently drowned, and following her mother's death, she made a solemn vow with her sister Ellen never to marry. Years later, John Meredith met her by a spring in Rainbow Valley and walked her home, sparking rumors of a romance. After comforting Mr. Meredith's daughter Faith over a lost pet, Rosemary was unexpectedly proposed to by Mr. Meredith; realizing she loved him, she asked for time to consider, but Ellen fiercely refused to release her from her vow, forcing Rosemary to send him a cold rejection. Later, after Norman Douglas asked Rosemary to release Ellen from her vow so they could wed, Rosemary agreed, but Ellen ultimately refused to marry Norman if it meant leaving Rosemary to live alone. Finally, Mr. Meredith's daughter Una visited Rosemary to ask her to marry her father, prompting Rosemary to give Una a note for him that restored his spirits.

value: Roy Gardner said: "That ought to be sufficient introduction. My name is Royal Gardner. And you are the Miss Shirley who read the Tennyson paper at the Philomathic the other evening, aren’t you?"

label: History
value: Ruby Gillis grew up with many big sisters.
unit: Ruby Gillis grew up with many big sisters and once used a magic pebble to charm away her warts. During her school days, she formed a Story Club alongside Anne and Jane Andrews. Ruby expressed a childhood wish to have dozens of beaus when she grew up, and she visited Boston the fall before falling ill. During Anne's time at Redmond, Ruby sent updates from home in a bundle of letters. After Anne returned to Avonlea, she learned that Ruby was terminally ill with consumption, even though Ruby stubbornly insisted she was healthy during a visit at her home. Later, Ruby tearfully confessed her fear of dying to Anne during an evening together, but she passed away peacefully in her sleep the following night.

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "There’s a concert at Carmody and a party at White Sands. Herb Spencer’s going to take me. He’s my latest. Be sure to come up tomorrow. I’m dying for a good talk with you. I want to hear all about your doings at Redmond."

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "Me! Why, I’m perfectly well. I never felt better in my life. Of course, that congestion last winter pulled me down a little. But just see my color. I don’t look much like an invalid, I’m sure."

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "Anne, it won’t be long now before I’ll be lying over there. You and Diana and all the rest will be going about, full of life—and I’ll be there—in the old graveyard—dead!"

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "I’ll try. I’ll think over what you have said, and try to believe it. And you’ll come up as often as you can, won’t you, Anne?"

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: “Nor I,” said Ruby Gillis, with a shiver. “I don’t mind floating down when there’s two or three of us in the flat and we can sit up. It’s fun then. But to lie down and pretend I was dead—I just couldn’t. I’d die really of fright.”

label: History
value: Twenty years prior, Sarah liked Luther Wallace.
unit: Twenty years prior, Sarah liked Luther Wallace, but her father sent him away because he was poor. Every spring, she was forced to whitewash an old duckhouse on her property that her father kept in case it became useful. When Anne Shirley got trapped in the duckhouse roof while trying to look in Sarah's pantry window, Sarah returned home after a rainstorm and freed her. After hearing Anne's explanation and sharing tea with her, Sarah agreed to sell Anne a blue willow-ware platter for twenty-five dollars.

label: History
value: Stella Maynard attended Queen's Academy
unit: Stella Maynard attended Queen's Academy with Anne and Priscilla and worked as a schoolteacher before entering Redmond College. After Anne's initial period of teaching, Stella received a letter from her sharing humorous anecdotes about her students. During her college years, Stella lived at Patty's Place with her friends, chatting about household matters and simple living alongside Aunt Jamesina and Phil. In her final year at Redmond, she reminisced with Anne over old Story Club manuscripts during a rainy evening of studying. Following final examinations, Stella and her housemates gathered to reflect on the life lessons and common sense they gained over their four years at college before packing up to leave Patty's Place after graduation.

label: Quote
value: Stella Maynard said: "I love Anne and I like Roy. Everybody says she is making a brilliant match, and even Mrs. Gardner thinks her charming now. It all sounds as if it were made in heaven, but I have my doubts. Make the most of that, Aunt Jamesina."

label: Quote
value: Stella Maynard said: “Well, I don’t know how he and the Sarah-cat will ever make out to live together,” said Stella pesimistically. “Cat-fights in the orchard o’nights are bad enough. But cat-fights here in the livingroom are unthinkable.”

label: Quote
value: Stella Maynard said: "I was afraid they’d come back. And then our jolly little nest here would be broken up—and we poor callow nestlings thrown out on the cruel world of boardinghouses again."

label: Quote
value: Stella Maynard said: "Nothing seems worthwhile. My very thoughts are old. I’ve thought them all before. What is the use of living after all, Anne?"

label: Quote
value: Stella Maynard said: "Oh, my mind agrees with you, Anne. But my soul remains doleful and uninspired. I’m always grubby and dingy on rainy nights."

label: History
value: Susan Baker never had a beau
unit: Susan Baker, an old maid who never had a beau or married despite liking men and being willing to marry, served as household help for Gilbert and Anne Blythe. After Anne gave birth to a healthy baby boy named James Matthew, Susan, alongside friends and family, visited to admire the newborn and celebrate his arrival. When a general election resulted in a Liberal victory, Captain Jim brought the news to Susan and Anne. Following a temporary absence to care for her injured sister, Susan returned from the Glen with news and commentary, and she later discussed the Blythes' upcoming move to the Glen with Anne and Leslie. At Ingleside, Susan cared for the family's children and routinely discussed local gossip with Anne and Cornelia Bryant, including the antics of the new minister's unruly children. She defended the children when Cornelia brought news of Faith Meredith's pig-riding escapade and later participated in conversations regarding town events and church politics. During one evening when the Meredith children panicked over seeing a supposed ghost in a sheet, Susan investigated the scene armed with a pitchfork and uncovered the mortifying truth that it was merely Mrs. Stimson searching for a lost knitting needle. Eventually, Susan, Anne, and Miss Cornelia gathered in the evening to discuss arrangements for the children ahead of an upcoming double wedding.

label: History
value: Una Meredith lived in Maywater
unit: Una Meredith lived in Maywater before moving to Glen St. Mary, having lost her mother when she was six years old. In Glen St. Mary, Una and her siblings quickly bonded with the Blythe children after meeting them in Rainbow Valley. When the Meredith children discovered a runaway orphan named Mary Vance in a barn, Una helped arrange a bed for her in the garret and comforted her when she cried. Encouraged by Nan Blythe, Una later visited Cornelia Bryant to ask if she would adopt Mary, which Cornelia accepted. Following a warning from Mary about their father possibly remarrying, Una became terrified of getting a stepmother. To improve their behavior and protect their father's reputation, Una and her siblings joined the Good-Conduct Club. During a club-mandated day of fasting, Una fainted during a church service, leaving her father overcome with guilt. Despite her deep fear of stepmothers, Una eventually visited Rosemary West to ask her to marry her father for his happiness, receiving reassurances of friendship from Rosemary and delivering a note that restored her father's spirits.

value: Uncle Jim is a homely man.
unit: Uncle Jim is a homely man with a tall, ungainly, and somewhat stooped figure that nevertheless suggests great strength and endurance. His clean-shaven face is deeply lined and bronzed, featuring spare jaws, a rugged mouth, a square brow, and clear, remarkably deep-set blue eyes that sometimes twinkle or dream. He has a thick mane of iron-gray hair falling to his shoulders, though as he grew older, his hair turned much grayer, his hand shook slightly, and he appeared frail and bent.

label: History
value: Uncle Jim is from a line of sea-going relatives on his mother's side.
unit: As a young man who hailed from a line of sea-going relatives on his mother's side, Uncle Jim ran off to sea and spent years sailing around the world, collecting material and curiosities from his travels. He welcomed Anne and Gilbert Blythe upon their arrival in Four Winds, quickly bonding with them and introducing Anne to the lighthouse. Uncle Jim shared his personal life-book with Owen Ford, who turned the captain's extraordinary life stories and the tragedy of his lost sweetheart into a published novel. He offered spiritual comfort to Anne during her grief, provided a mortgage to assist with a medical procedure for Leslie, and was honored when Anne and Gilbert named their newborn son James Matthew after him. Before his death, Uncle Jim entrusted his cat First Mate to Anne's care, gave his blessing to Leslie and Owen's romance, and bequeathed his museum of curiosities to young Jem. He passed away peacefully on his sofa after receiving and reading the completed print copy of his life story.

label: Quote
value: Uncle Jim said: "Nephew Alec. He understands it as well as I do. Well, now, I’m real glad you asked me to stay to supper. I’m proper hungry—didn’t have much of a dinner today."

label: Quote
value: Uncle Jim said: “Oh, I do, Mistress Doctor, I do,” protested Captain Jim. “Why, I live like a king gen’rally. Last night I was up to the Glen and took home two pounds of steak. I meant to have a spanking good dinner today.”

label: Quote
value: Uncle Jim said: "The Government don’t give lighthouse keepers such luxuries. Look at the colors that wood makes. If you’d like some driftwood for your fire, Mistress Blythe, I’ll bring you up a load some day. Sit down. I’m going to make you a cup of tea."

label: Quote
value: Uncle Jim said: "That’s Marshall Elliott—a mighty fine man with jest one streak of foolishness in him. I s’pose you wondered what his object was in turning himself into a sort of dime museum freak."

label: Quote
value: Uncle Jim said: "Yes, I called in on my way home to see him. He’s getting round all right—but stewing in a broth of trouble, as usual, poor man."

unit: While Mr. Meredith and Jerry are away and Aunt Martha is bedridden, Faith and Una try to manage the house, attend a empty Sunday School, and clean the manse the following day. Faith's rug-shaking in the graveyard on Monday leads to local rumors and scandal among churchgoers. Meanwhile, Carl falls sick, but Aunt Martha recovers and the Blythes return home shortly after.

label: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
value: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans.
chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans on their drive home from Carmody when they spot a Jersey cow trampling Mr. Harrison's oat field. Believing the cow is her own nuisance Jersey, Dolly, Anne impulsively sells the stray cow on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning to Green Gables, Anne discovers Dolly still in the barnyard and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow, prompting her to head over to his house with the money and a cake to confess.

chapter: v3 · Chapter I The Shadow of Change
unit: Anne and Diana chat about growing up and upcoming changes as they rest in the orchard. After getting a letter from Priscilla Grant, Anne meets Gilbert on the bridge, but she gets flustered and cuts the moment short when he touches her hand. Returning to Green Gables, she comforts Davy Keith and talks with him before spending a quiet moment dreaming by the brook.

unit: Anne leaves Green Gables amidst tearful goodbyes and travels by train and boat to Kingsport alongside Gilbert and Charlie. Upon arriving, she is greeted by Priscilla Grant, who takes her to their new boardinghouse while chatting gaily to lift her homesick spirits.

unit: Anne returns to Avonlea and learns from Mrs. Lynde that Ruby Gillis is terminally ill with consumption. They then visit the Gillis household, finding a lively crowd and Ruby stubbornly insisting she is perfectly healthy despite her failing condition.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXXVIII. The Bend in the Road
unit: Marilla learns from an oculist that she must give up heavy eye work or face total blindness, putting the future of Green Gables in jeopardy. Anne decides to forfeit her college scholarship, stay at home to care for Marilla, and take up a local teaching job instead. After learning Gilbert Blythe gave up the Avonlea school so she could have it, Anne meets Gilbert on her way home and they finally end their feud to become close friends.

label: v2 · VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women
value: Anne and Diana continue canvassing Avonlea for subscriptions
chapter: v2 · VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women

chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans on their drive home from Carmody when they spot a Jersey cow trampling Mr. Harrison's oat field. Believing the cow is her own nuisance Jersey, Dolly, Anne impulsively sells the stray cow on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning to Green Gables, Anne discovers Dolly still in the barnyard and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow, prompting her to head over to his house with the money and a cake to confess.

unit: On the eve of the school term, Anne discusses teaching methods and classroom discipline with Jane and Gilbert, strongly opposing corporal punishment. The next morning, a nervous Anne drinks ginger tea prepared by Marilla before starting her first day of teaching.

unit: Anne and Diana continue canvassing Avonlea for subscriptions, encountering peculiar neighbors like the hyper-neat Mrs. Theodore White and receiving mixed results. unit: Marilla learns from an oculist that she must give up heavy eye work or face total blindness, putting the future of Green Gables in jeopardy. After learning Gilbert Blythe gave up the Avonlea school so she could have it, Anne meets Gilbert on her way home and they finally end their feud to become close friends.

chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans on their drive home from Carmody when they spot a Jersey cow trampling Mr. Harrison's oat field. Believing the cow is her own nuisance Jersey, Dolly, Anne impulsively sells the stray cow on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning to Green Gables, Anne discovers Dolly still in the barnyard and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow, prompting her to head over to his house with the money and a cake to confess.

unit: On the eve of the school term, Anne discusses teaching methods and classroom discipline with Jane and Gilbert, strongly opposing corporal punishment. The next morning, a nervous Anne drinks ginger tea prepared by Marilla before starting her first day of teaching.

He seeks help from Mrs. Lynde, who agrees to buy and sew a stylish brown dress with puffed sleeves for Anne. On Christmas morning, Anne is overjoyed to receive the dress from Matthew, along with a pair of slippers sent by Aunt Josephine.

label: v1 · CHAPTER XXVII. Vanity and Vexation of Spirit
value: Marilla returns home to Green Gables.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXVII. Vanity and Vexation of Spirit
unit: Marilla returns home to Green Gables expecting supper, but finds the stove unlit and Anne nowhere in sight. When Marilla goes upstairs, she discovers Anne hiding under her pillows because she dyed her red hair green using hair dye bought from a peddler. After washing fails to remove the green color, Marilla cuts Anne's hair off short, leaving Anne to reflect remorsefully on her vanity.

unit: Diana helps Anne dress in her east gable room before driving to the White Sands Hotel for a benefit concert with Jane and Billy Andrews. chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans on their drive home from Carmody when they spot a Jersey cow trampling Mr. Harrison's oat field. Believing the cow is her own nuisance Jersey, Dolly, Anne impulsively sells the stray cow on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning to Green Gables, Anne discovers Dolly still in the barnyard and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow, prompting her to head over to his house with the money and a cake to confess.

Upon returning to Green Gables, Anne discovers Dolly still in the barnyard and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow, prompting her to head over to his house with the money and a cake to confess.

Marilla consults Rachel Lynde, who advises letting Anne cool off at home for a while. Later, Marilla is overcome with laughter when she finds Anne weeping over an imagined future scenario where Diana gets married and leaves her.

unit: Anne and her friends re-enact a poem on a flat-bottomed boat, but the boat begins to leak, stranding Anne on a bridge pile. After returning home safely, Anne reflects on learning another lesson, while Matthew quietly encourages her not to abandon all her romance.

value: Anne and Priscilla settle into college life at Redmond
chapter: v3 · Chapter V Letters from Home
unit: Anne and Priscilla settle into college life at Redmond as their freshman class wins the annual Arts Rush under Gilbert Blythe's leadership. Anne receives a bundle of letters from home—including updates from Jane, Ruby, Diana, Marilla, Mrs. Lynde, and Davy—which helps connect her old life in Avonlea to her new life in Kingsport.

unit: Faith is furious with Aunt Martha for killing her pet rooster, Adam, to feed the visiting minister, Mr. Perry. value: Faith gives her shoes to Lida Marsh.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XXIV. A CHARITABLE IMPULSE
unit: Faith gives her shoes and good stockings to a cold, barefoot girl named Lida Marsh, only to realize afterwards that her only remaining option for Sunday church is a hideous pair of striped stockings. Refusing to wear them or fake an illness, Faith stands on a snowbank trying to catch a cold so she can legitimately stay home. Jerry and Una forcibly pull Faith off the snow while passing townspeople overhear their noisy argument.

unit: The Meredith children gather in the old Methodist graveyard and chat about their lives and local gossip. chapter: v5 · CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY VANCE
unit: The Meredith children discover Mary Vance, a hungry runaway orphan, hiding in a nearby barn loft. After feeding her at the manse, they listen to her tragic backstory and teach her about religious concepts in the graveyard. Faith lends her clean clothes, and the children take her to Rainbow Valley before finding her a place to sleep in their garret.

unit: After Cornelia Bryant cautions Mr. Meredith about Mary Vance, Mr. Meredith speaks kindly to Mary and alleviates her fears. value: Mr. Meredith is away
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE
unit: While Mr. Meredith and Jerry are away and Aunt Martha is bedridden, Faith and Una try to manage the house, attend a empty Sunday School, and clean the manse the following day. Faith's rug-shaking in the graveyard on Monday leads to local rumors and scandal among churchgoers. Meanwhile, Carl falls sick, but Aunt Martha recovers and the Blythes return home shortly after.

Inspired by Jem's advice, Faith, Jerry, Una, and Carl agree to form the club to manage their own conduct.

value: Faith causes a scandal in Glen St.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XXV. ANOTHER SCANDAL AND ANOTHER “EXPLANATION”
unit: Faith causes a scandal in Glen St. Mary by attending church without stockings, sparking community gossip and concern among Susan Baker and Miss Cornelia. To clear her father of any blame, Faith writes a detailed letter of explanation to the local newspaper.

value: Faith is furious with Aunt Martha
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XIX. POOR ADAM!
unit: Faith is furious with Aunt Martha for killing her pet rooster, Adam, to feed the visiting minister, Mr. Perry. During dinner and a subsequent conversation in the study, Faith deeply dislikes the pompous Mr. Perry for his condescending lecture. When his coat-tails catch fire from the hearth, Faith deliberately refrains from interrupting him, leaving Mr. Perry enraged and his coat scorched.

label: v5 · CHAPTER XXV. ANOTHER SCANDAL AND ANOTHER “EXPLANATION”
value: Faith causes a scandal in Glen St. Mary.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XXV. ANOTHER SCANDAL AND ANOTHER “EXPLANATION”
unit: Faith causes a scandal in Glen St. Mary by attending church without stockings, sparking community gossip and concern among Susan Baker and Miss Cornelia. In Rainbow Valley, the other children discuss the incident, and Jerry punishes Faith via the Good-Conduct Club by making her wear her hated striped stockings. To clear her father of any blame, Faith writes a detailed letter of explanation to the local newspaper.

chapter: v2 · XXI Sweet Miss Lavendar

value: Faith gives her shoes to Lida Marsh.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XXIV. A CHARITABLE IMPULSE
unit: Faith gives her shoes and good stockings to a cold, barefoot girl named Lida Marsh, only to realize afterwards that her only remaining option for Sunday church is a hideous pair of striped stockings. Refusing to wear them or fake an illness, Faith stands on a snowbank trying to catch a cold so she can legitimately stay home. Jerry and Una forcibly pull Faith off the snow while passing townspeople overhear their noisy argument.

value: Faith causes a scandal in Glen St.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XXV. ANOTHER SCANDAL AND ANOTHER “EXPLANATION”
unit: Faith causes a scandal in Glen St. Mary by attending church without stockings, sparking community gossip and concern among Susan Baker and Miss Cornelia. In Rainbow Valley, the other children discuss the incident, and Jerry punishes Faith via the Good-Conduct Club by making her wear her hated striped stockings. To clear her father of any blame, Faith writes a detailed letter of explanation to the local newspaper.

value: Anne discusses teaching methods with Jane and Gilbert.
chapter: v2 · IV Different Opinions
unit: On the eve of the school term, Anne discusses teaching methods and classroom discipline with Jane and Gilbert, strongly opposing corporal punishment. After returning to Green Gables, she visits Mr. Harrison, who also doubts her plan to rule by affection rather than the rod. The next morning, a nervous Anne drinks ginger tea prepared by Marilla before starting her first day of teaching.

unit: Anne and Diana continue canvassing Avonlea for subscriptions, encountering peculiar neighbors like the hyper-neat Mrs. Theodore White and receiving mixed results. Learning that Lorenzo White just had a new baby boy, Anne strategically visits him while he is overjoyed, securing a generous five-dollar donation. Later that evening, Anne visits Mr. Harrison to ask for a contribution, but he flatly refuses.

chapter: v3 · Chapter V Letters from Home
unit: Anne and Priscilla settle into college life at Redmond as their freshman class wins the annual Arts Rush under Gilbert Blythe's leadership. Philippa Gordon quickly adopts Anne and Priscilla, introducing them into Redmond's active social circle. Anne receives a bundle of letters from home—including updates from Jane, Ruby, Diana, Marilla, Mrs. Lynde, and Davy—which helps connect her old life in Avonlea to her new life in Kingsport.

unit: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans on their drive home from Carmody when they spot a Jersey cow trampling Mr. Harrison's oat field. Believing the cow is her own nuisance Jersey, Dolly, Anne impulsively sells the stray cow on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning to Green Gables, Anne discovers Dolly still in the barnyard and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow, prompting her to head over to his house with the money and a cake to confess.

chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans on their drive home from Carmody when they spot a Jersey cow trampling Mr. Harrison's oat field. Believing the cow is her own nuisance Jersey, Dolly, Anne impulsively sells the stray cow on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning to Green Gables, Anne discovers Dolly still in the barnyard and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow, prompting her to head over to his house with the money and a cake to confess.

Upon returning to Green Gables, Anne discovers Dolly still in the barnyard and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow, prompting her to head over to his house with the money and a cake to confess.

unit: Marilla returns home to Green Gables expecting supper, but finds the stove unlit and Anne nowhere in sight. After washing fails to remove the green color, Marilla cuts Anne's hair off short, leaving Anne to reflect remorsefully on her vanity.

section: II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
label: II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
value: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans.
chapter: II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans on their drive home from Carmody when they spot a Jersey cow trampling Mr. Harrison's oat field. unit: Faith gives her shoes and good stockings to a cold, barefoot girl named Lida Marsh, only to realize afterwards that her only remaining option for Sunday church is a hideous pair of striped stockings. Jerry and Una forcibly pull Faith off the snow while passing townspeople overhear their noisy argument.
